card.name: Pearson's chi-squared test (1900)
card.definition: Pearson's 1900 test quantifies distributional mismatch as the sum over categories of (observed-expected)^2/expected and tests goodness of fit.

card.name: Pearson's chi-squared goodness-of-fit test (1900)
card.definition: Karl Pearson published his chi-squared test in 1900, comparing observed frequencies with expected frequencies under a hypothesised distribution.

card.name: Fisher's maximum likelihood estimation (1922)
card.definition: Fisher's 1922 paper formalized choosing parameters that maximize the likelihood, in practice its logarithm, of the observed data under the model.

card.name: Fisher's maximum likelihood (1922)
card.definition: R. A. Fisher introduced the method of maximum likelihood in its modern form in 1922, after first presenting a numerical procedure in 1912.

note: gray-zone band 0.80-0.92; adjudicate SAME / DIFFERENT / SUBTYPE

card.name: Huygens's expectation (1657)
card.definition: Huygens's De Ratiociniis in Ludo Aleae (1657), the first printed probability textbook, formalized expectation as the probability-weighted value of an uncertain prospect.

card.name: Huygens's mathematical expectation (1657)
card.definition: Christiaan Huygens published De ratiociniis in aleae ludo in 1657, the first published book on probability, systematising expectation.

card.name: Bernoulli's Ars Conjectandi and law of large numbers (1713)
card.definition: Jacob Bernoulli's posthumous Ars Conjectandi (1713) proved the law of large numbers, that observed frequencies converge to the true probability.

card.name: Bernoulli's Ars Conjectandi (1713)
card.definition: Jacob Bernoulli's Ars Conjectandi was published posthumously in 1713 and contained the first version of the law of large numbers.
